name: Gettysburg National Military Park
description: Site of the Battle of Gettysburg, fought July 1-3, 1863. The largest and bloodiest battle of the Civil War, often considered the turning point of the conflict.
historical_significance: Turning point of the Civil War. Site of Pickett's Charge and Lincoln's Gettysburg Address delivered on November 19, 1863.
current_status: National Park Service site - well preserved battlefield

name: Fort Sumter National Monument
description: A sea fort in Charleston Harbor where the first shots of the Civil War were fired on April 12, 1861.
historical_significance: Site where the Civil War began. The Confederate bombardment of Fort Sumter marked the start of open hostilities.
current_status: National Park Service site - accessible by ferry

name: Antietam National Battlefield
description: Site of the Battle of Antietam on September 17, 1862, the bloodiest single-day battle in American history.
historical_significance: Bloodiest single-day battle in American history with over 22,000 casualties. Union victory led to the Emancipation Proclamation.
current_status: National Park Service site - well preserved battlefield

name: Vicksburg National Military Park
description: Site of the Siege of Vicksburg, May 18 - July 4, 1863. The Union victory gave complete control of the Mississippi River.
historical_significance: Key Union victory that split the Confederacy by giving control of the Mississippi River. Fell on July 4, 1863, the day after Gettysburg.
current_status: National Park Service site - includes USS Cairo museum

name: Appomattox Court House National Historical Park
description: Site where General Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant on April 9, 1865.
historical_significance: Location of Lee's surrender to Grant, effectively ending the Civil War. The surrender occurred in the McLean House.
current_status: National Park Service site - reconstructed village

name: Manassas National Battlefield Park
description: Site of two major Civil War battles: First Battle of Bull Run (July 21, 1861) and Second Battle of Bull Run (August 28-30, 1862).
historical_significance: Site of the first major land battle of the Civil War and a second major Confederate victory in 1862.
current_status: National Park Service site - well preserved battlefield

name: Shiloh National Military Park
description: Site of the Battle of Shiloh, April 6-7, 1862. One of the bloodiest battles of the Western Theater.
historical_significance: Major early Union victory in the Western Theater. Confederate General Albert Sidney Johnston was killed here.

name: Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park
description: America's first and largest military park, preserving the sites of the Battles of Chickamauga (September 1863) and Chattanooga (November 1863).
historical_significance: Site of the second bloodiest battle of the Civil War and the Union's subsequent 'Battle Above the Clouds' at Chattanooga.
current_status: National Park Service site - first national military park established

name: Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania National Military Park
description: Site of four major Civil War battles: Fredericksburg, Chancellorsville, Wilderness, and Spotsylvania Court House.
historical_significance: Preserves four major battlefields. Site where Stonewall Jackson was mortally wounded at Chancellorsville.

name: Petersburg National Battlefield
description: Site of the Siege of Petersburg, June 1864 - April 1865. The longest siege of the Civil War.
historical_significance: Ten-month siege that ultimately led to the fall of Richmond and Lee's surrender at Appomattox.

name: Richmond National Battlefield Park
description: Preserves 13 sites associated with the Union campaigns to capture Richmond, the Confederate capital.
historical_significance: Capital of the Confederacy. Site of numerous battles including the Seven Days Battles and Cold Harbor.

name: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park
description: Site of John Brown's 1859 raid on the federal armory, a precursor to the Civil War. Changed hands eight times during the war.
historical_significance: Site of John Brown's raid. Strategic location at the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers changed hands multiple times.

name: Ford's Theatre National Historic Site
description: Site where President Abraham Lincoln was assassinated by John Wilkes Booth on April 14, 1865.
historical_significance: Site of Lincoln's assassination, five days after Lee's surrender at Appomattox. Lincoln died the next morning at the Petersen House across the street.
current_status: National Park Service site - operating theater
